title: Equilibrium flow maps for text (LM1B)
headline: gen_ppl_1

views.title: Perplexity of one-step samples (void if entropy < 3.9)
views.shows: $\mathrm{PPL} = \exp\big(-\frac{1}{N}\sum_n \log p_{\mathrm{GPT2L}}(w_n \mid w_{<n})\big)$ over the judge tokens $w$ of 1024 samples, sampler with $K = 1$ jump
views.label: Perplexity of one-step samples (void if entropy < 3.9)
views.meaning: perplexity of one-step samples under GPT-2 Large (real text: 52.7). Void when the entropy of the same samples is below 3.9: the samples repeat one token, which GPT-2 predicts easily, so a value near 1 is a collapse, not a good result.

views.title: Entropy of one-step samples
views.shows: $H$ = mean over 1024 samples of $-\sum_v q_v \log q_v$, $q_v$ = frequency of token $v$ in the sample, $K = 1$
views.label: Entropy of one-step samples
views.meaning: token entropy inside one sample; real text is 4.31. Below 3.9 the samples are repetitive and their perplexity is void; near 0 the model outputs one repeated token.

views.title: Perplexity of 8-step samples (void if entropy < 3.9)
views.shows: $\mathrm{PPL} = \exp\big(-\frac{1}{N}\sum_n \log p_{\mathrm{GPT2L}}(w_n \mid w_{<n})\big)$ over the judge tokens $w$ of 1024 samples, $K = 8$ jumps, churn $g = 0$
views.label: Perplexity of 8-step samples (void if entropy < 3.9)
views.meaning: perplexity of 8-step samples, deterministic sampler. Void when the entropy of the same samples is below 3.9: the samples repeat one token, which GPT-2 predicts easily, so a value near 1 is a collapse, not a good result.

views.title: Perplexity of 8-step samples, stochastic sampler (void if entropy < 3.9)
views.shows: $\mathrm{PPL} = \exp\big(-\frac{1}{N}\sum_n \log p_{\mathrm{GPT2L}}(w_n \mid w_{<n})\big)$ over the judge tokens $w$ of 1024 samples, $K = 8$ jumps, churn $g = 0.8$

views.meaning: perplexity of 8-step samples with the stochastic sampler of FMLM. Void when the entropy of the same samples is below 3.9: the samples repeat one token, which GPT-2 predicts easily, so a value near 1 is a collapse, not a good result.

views.title: Perplexity of 1024-step samples (void if entropy < 3.9)
views.shows: $\mathrm{PPL} = \exp\big(-\frac{1}{N}\sum_n \log p_{\mathrm{GPT2L}}(w_n \mid w_{<n})\big)$ over the judge tokens $w$ of 1024 samples, Euler sampler of $\hat D$ with $K = 1024$
views.label: Perplexity of 1024-step samples (void if entropy < 3.9)
views.meaning: perplexity of a denoiser sampled with 1024 Euler steps. Void when the entropy of the same samples is below 3.9: the samples repeat one token, which GPT-2 predicts easily, so a value near 1 is a collapse, not a good result.

views.title: Training loss
views.shows: $L = w_{\mathrm{diag}} L_{\mathrm{diag}} + \alpha L_{\mathrm{off}}$ (flow map) or $L_{\mathrm{diag}}$ (denoiser), mean over the last `train.log_every` steps
views.label: Training loss
views.meaning: training loss, averaged over the last log interval

algos.denoiser: $\hat D = \arg\min \mathbb{E}_{t,x_0,x_1}\big[-w(t)\, x_1 \cdot \log \hat D(I_t)\big]$, $I_t = (1-t)x_0 + t x_1$; sampled by Euler steps of $\dot x = (\hat D(x) - x)/(1-t)$
algos.flow-map: $\hat\Phi_\kappa(x) = (1-\kappa)x + \kappa\,\hat\delta_\kappa(x)$ with $\hat\delta_0 = \hat D$ and $\hat\delta_\kappa$ trained by cross-entropy to a stop-gradient target (semigroup, Lagrangian or Eulerian); sampled by $K$ jumps

params.out_dir: folder for logs and results of the run
params.clock: map between the label $\sigma$ and $\kappa$: exponential $\kappa = \sigma$, $c = 1-\sigma$; rational $\kappa = 1 - e^{-\sigma/(1-\sigma)}$, $c = (1-\sigma)^2$
params.data.name: dataset: toy (8 fixed sequences), text (characters), tokens (token file), blocks (LM1B cut in sequences of $L$ tokens as in FLM)
params.data.n_modes: number of sequences of the toy data
params.model.arch: network: denoiser (small transformer, absolute positions) or dit (the 12-layer transformer of FLM, rotary positions)
params.model.mlp_ratio: hidden width of the feed-forward layers divided by `model.dim`
params.model.sigma_scale: denoiser arch: largest frequency of the embedding of $\sigma$, in radians per unit $\sigma$
params.model.cond: inputs of the network besides $x$: duration $\to \sigma$; state_time $\to \tau(\hat t(x))$ and $\tau(t')$ (time-free); time $\to \tau(t)$ and $\tau(t')$ (FLM, FMLM)
params.model.cond_dim: width of the embedding of the scalar inputs (dit)
params.loss.diag_time: law of $t$ and weight $w(t)$ of the diagonal loss: uniform $t \sim \mathcal{U}[0,1-\epsilon]$, $w = \frac{1}{1-t}$; log_uniform density $\propto \frac{1}{1-t}$, $w$ constant; reparam $\tau(t) \sim \mathcal{U}[0,1]$, $w = 1$
params.loss.stratified: if true, the $B$ uniform draws of a batch are $u_i = (i + \mathcal{U}[0,1])/B$ in random order
params.loss.t_eps: $\epsilon$: largest time is $1 - \epsilon$ in `loss.diag_time` = uniform or log_uniform
params.loss.off_diagonal: target $\bar\delta$: semigroup $\gamma\hat\delta_{\kappa_1}(x) + (1-\gamma)\hat\delta_{\kappa_2}(\hat\Phi_{\kappa_1}(x))$; lagrangian $\bar D(\hat\Phi_\kappa(x)) - c\kappa\,\partial_\sigma\hat\delta$; eulerian $(1-\kappa)\bar D(x) + \kappa(\hat\delta + J)$
params.loss.diag_weight: $w_{\mathrm{diag}}$ in $L = w_{\mathrm{diag}}L_{\mathrm{diag}} + \alpha L_{\mathrm{off}}$; 0 trains no denoiser
params.loss.direction: Eulerian loss: $J$ is the derivative of $\hat\delta$ along $(\bar D(x) - x, -c)$ (denoiser) or along $(x_1 - x, -c)$ (data)
params.loss.jvp: how derivatives of $\hat\delta$ are computed: forward (forward-mode differentiation) or fd (central finite differences)
params.loss.fd_eps: step $h$ of the finite difference $\frac{f(z + hu) - f(z - hu)}{2h}$
params.loss.split_batch: if true, the first half of the batch is used for $L_{\mathrm{diag}}$ and the second for $L_{\mathrm{off}}$
params.loss.teacher: checkpoint of the frozen denoiser $\bar D$ (distillation); none: training from data, $\bar D = \hat\delta_0$
params.loss.teacher_cond: how the teacher is told the time (same choices as `model.cond`)
params.loss.init_from_teacher: if true, the flow map starts from the teacher's weights
params.loss.flat_init: duration-conditioned dit: start with $\hat\delta_\sigma = \bar D$ for every $\sigma$
params.loss.jump_sampling: law of $(t, \kappa)$: notes $t, \sigma \sim \mathcal{U}[0,1]$; reparam $h \sim \mathcal{U}[0,1]$, $\tau(t) \sim \mathcal{U}[0,1-h]$, $\tau(t') = \tau(t) + h$; endpoint $t \sim \mathcal{U}[0,1]$, $\kappa = 1$
params.loss.whole_jump_prob: probability that an off-diagonal sample is the whole jump $t = 0$, $\kappa = 1$ (reparam sampling)
params.loss.whole_jump_target: target for samples with $\kappa = 1$ under the Lagrangian or Eulerian loss: same, or the semigroup target
params.loss.boundary_prob: probability that an off-diagonal sample is a boundary sample: $t \sim \mathcal{U}[t_b, 1]$, any $\kappa$, target $\bar D(I_t)$
params.loss.boundary_t: $t_b$: smallest time of a boundary sample
params.loss.boundary_target: target of a boundary sample: $\bar D(I_t)$ (denoiser) or $x_1$ (data)
params.train.batch_size: $B$ per process; the batch of one step is $B \times$ processes $\times$ `train.grad_accum`
params.train.grad_accum: number of batches whose gradients are summed per optimizer step
params.train.lr: $\eta$: learning rate of AdamW after warmup
params.train.warmup: $W$: learning rate at step $k$ is $\eta\min(1, k/W)$
params.train.grad_clip: largest norm of the gradient (0: no clipping)
params.train.ema: $\rho$: averaged weights $\bar\theta \leftarrow \rho\bar\theta + (1-\rho)\theta$; samples and teachers use $\bar\theta$
params.train.precision: mixed precision passed to accelerate (the dit runs its blocks in bfloat16 by itself)
params.train.resume: if true, continue from the last checkpoint of `ckpt_dir`
params.train.init: checkpoint whose averaged weights initialise the network
params.train.init_time: value of $\tau$ at which a time-conditioned initialisation is frozen when the new network is time-free
params.train.min_rate: stop and move to another node if the speed is below this many steps per second (0: off)
params.train.max_minutes: checkpoint and stop after this many minutes (0: off)
params.train.keep_every: steps between two kept copies of the averaged weights (0: off)
params.eval.grid: sampling times $t_0 = 0 < \dots < t_K = 1$: uniform $t_k = k/K$; reparam $\tau(t_k) = k/K$; $\kappa_k = \frac{t_{k+1} - t_k}{1 - t_k}$
params.eval.judge: language model that scores the samples
params.wandb.name: Weights and Biases run name
params.loss.end_jump_prob: probability that an off-diagonal sample is a jump to the end: $\tau(t) \sim \mathcal{U}[0,1]$, $\kappa = 1$ (reparam sampling)
params.train.lr_decay: none: constant $\eta$ after warmup; cosine: $\eta_k = \frac{\eta}{2}(1 + \cos(\pi k / K_{\mathrm{train}}))$, $K_{\mathrm{train}}$ = `train.steps`
params.loss.target_net: weights used inside the target $\bar\delta$: online $\theta$, or ema $\bar\theta$ (the running average, which moves slowly)
params.loss.target_eval: if true, the target $\bar\delta$ is computed without dropout
params.loss.partial_context: if true, per sample a fraction $f \sim \mathcal{U}[0,1]$ of the positions is clean context: $t^l = 1$ with probability $f$, else $t^l = t$ (DBTM)
params.loss.ril_frac: fraction of the batch used for refinement in the loop (DBTM); 0: off
params.loss.ril_depth: $k$: number of refinement rounds in the training rollout
params.loss.ril_threshold: commit threshold: a position is committed when the probability of its token is at least this value
params.loss.ril_weight: weight of the refinement loss $L_{\mathrm{ril}}$ in the total loss
params.loss.ril_ot: if true, noise and data of the rollout are paired by minibatch optimal transport
params.loss.ril_distill_weight: weight of the self-distillation loss of the rollout (target: a frozen copy of the model at the last round)
params.loss.ril_distill_start: training step at which the self-distillation loss starts
params.loss.ril_distill_temp: temperature $T$ of the self-distillation target, softmax(logits $/ T$)
params.loss.ril_refresh: steps between two refreshes of the frozen copy used as self-distillation teacher

symbols.x_1: one-hot matrix in $\mathbb{R}^{L \times V}$ of a data sequence $y$ of $L$ tokens from a vocabulary of size $V$
symbols.\\hat D: denoiser: softmax network, $\hat D(x) \approx \mathbb{E}[x_1 \mid I_t = x]$
symbols.\\kappa: jump fraction in $[0,1]$: a jump from time $t$ lands at $t' = 1 - (1-\kappa)(1-t)$; $\kappa = 1$ is the whole jump to the end
symbols.\\hat\\delta_\\kappa: softmax network of the flow map; one jump is $\hat\Phi_\kappa(x) = (1-\kappa)x + \kappa\hat\delta_\kappa(x)$, and $\hat\delta_0 = \hat D$
symbols.\\sigma: duration label seen by a duration-conditioned network, $\kappa = \kappa(\sigma)$ given by the clock
symbols.\\tau(t): decoding-error clock of FLM: $\tau(t) = 1 - \frac{V}{V-1}P(\arg\max_v I_t^l \ne y^l)$, increasing from 0 to 1
symbols.\\hat t(x): time read off a state: root of $(1-t)^2 V + t^2 = \frac{1}{L}\sum_l \lVert x^l \rVert^2$
symbols.\\bar D: denoiser used in targets, no gradient: the frozen teacher when distilling, else the model's own $\hat\delta_0$
symbols.\\mathrm{PPL}: generative perplexity of samples under GPT-2 Large, lower is better (real LM1B text: 52.7)
symbols.H: mean entropy of the token histogram of one sample, in nats (real LM1B text: 4.31); compare $\mathrm{PPL}$ only at similar $H$
symbols.g: churn of the sampler: fraction of fresh noise re-injected after each jump ($g = 0$: deterministic)

formula: $L = \mathbb{E}\big[-w(t)\, x_1 \cdot \log \hat\delta_0(I_t)\big] + \alpha\, \mathbb{E}\big[-\bar\delta \cdot \log \hat\delta_\kappa(I_t)\big]$, $I_t = (1-t)x_0 + t x_1$, $\bar\delta$ = stop-gradient target (semigroup, Lagrangian or Eulerian). Sampling: $x \leftarrow (1-\kappa_k)x + \kappa_k \hat\delta_{\kappa_k}(x)$, $k = 0..K-1$, $\kappa_{K-1} = 1$, output $\arg\max_v x^l_v$.
